messages:
chris: Quick postmortem follow-up from last night's cross-region traffic surge — we saw a short window (~09:12-09:22 UTC) where TLS handshakes retried heavily and routing diverged. I sketched a working hypothesis and action items below.

maria: TL;DR on root cause?

chris: Short version: two factors lined up — a) stale DNS responses from a regional registrar during a low-ttl rotation, b) a concurrent rollout that reordered a subset of route rules so some regions briefly pointed at a legacy pool that doesn't support the new SNI mapping. Retries amplified due to clients hitting fallback tiers.

alex: Ack. do we have packet-level evidence of SNI mismatch or is it inferred from handshake errors?

paul: I pulled the edge logs, 09:12:34 -> 09:14:10 shows repeated 421/timeout then TLS alert 40 (handshake_failure) and SNI "prod.v2" expected / actual "prod" in ~47% of sampled connections. attaching the excerpt:```edge.logExcerpt
[09:12:36] src=10.10.38.21 dst=lb-nyc-03 TLS_ALERT=40 SNI=prod
[09:12:37] src=10.10.38.21 dst=lb-nyc-03 TLS_ALERT=40 SNI=prod.v2
```

chris: thanks. timeline: deploy at 09:10 UTC triggered route-rule rollout at 09:11. registrar rotation with TTL enforcement happened 09:12. overlap window caused divergence.

infra-eng: Proposed mitigations: 1) revert the route-rule ordering patch to eliminate legacy pool traffic (short term), 2) enforce SNI-compatible health checks on pools, 3) add an evasive TTL guard to control registrar rotations during rollouts (longer term).

maria: Can we assign owners and dates? We need a clear runway before next deploy.

chris: Agreed. Draft action items: 
- AI-101: Revert route-rule ordering patch and redeploy (owner: alex) — ETA 2h.
- AI-102: Add SNI sanity check to pool health probe + quick fix to mark legacy pool unhealthy if SNI mismatch seen (owner: paul) — ETA EOD today.
- AI-103: Registrar TTL guard: small control-plane feature to delay registrar rotations while a rollout is in-flight (owner: infra-eng) — ETA next sprint (target 2 weeks).
- AI-104: Add monitoring rule for cross-region TLS handshake error rate spike (owner: sre-oncall / chris) — ETA 24h.

alex: Taking AI-101. I'll cut the rollback patch and coordinate with deploy-bot for an out-of-band deploy.

deploy-bot: @alex scheduled out-of-band deploy for rollback at 11:04 UTC. CI checklist passed.

paul: Taking AI-102. I'll push a heuristic to mark pools unhealthy on repeated SNI mismatch and open a short-lived flag for immediate rollout to Dedicated and Hosted.

sre-oncall: I'll own AI-104, adding an alert that fires at a 3x baseline TLS_handshake_failure rate for cross-region traffic for 5m. Also adding a dashboard row for SNI mismatch ratio.

maria: For AI-103 can infra-eng call out dependencies? registrar API has a 6s propagation on average — we need a rate-limiter and lock semantics in the control plane.

infra-eng: Yup. We'll propose a scheduler lock: if a rollout is active for a route, registrar rotations for that hostname are paused for +30s. Raises risk of slower rotation but prevents overlap. We'll draft the RFC by EOD and aim to ship the guard in the 2-week sprint.

chris: Good. Quick verification checklist: 
1) confirm rollback reduced retry rate (alex)
2) confirm SNI mismatch probe triggers on sample traffic (paul)
3) alert validates and no false positives (sre-oncall)
4) RFC for TTL guard (infra-eng)

alex: Update — rollback deployed at 11:04, initial metrics show retry rate dropped from 6.2% -> 0.9% within 3m. Pushing the datapoint to the incident dashboard.

paul: Probe patch in branch fix/sni-probe, tests green. Opening PR: https://git.redwood/infrapkg/pull/842. Will flag for hotfix merge once review done.

sre-oncall: Alert rule live in staging, firing correctly on synthetic repro. Will promote to prod after we confirm probe PR.

maria: Nice. Any persistent action for customers? Do we need a customer-facing note?

chris: No external impact reported beyond transient errors for a small % of requests. We'll keep it internal but mention in the next weekly ops digest.

paul: Quick follow-up: adding a small backoff jitter to client-facing edges to avoid retry storms if a region reports transient TLS failures. Might help similar patterns. Owner: paul, ETA: next week. 

infra-eng: Documenting the proposed TTL guard in the RFC will include a rollback safety checklist and metrics to monitor.

chris: Great progress. I'll capture these in the postmortem follow-up doc and update the incident tracker. Please update this thread when each AI is closed.

maria: Closing note: set recurring review for 'cross-region retry patterns' weekly for 3 weeks to capture regressions. Owner: chris.

sre-oncall: Noted, will add a calendar block. :white_check_mark:

alex: marking AI-101 done in tracker.

paul: PR opened for AI-102.

chris: thanks everyone — keeping this thread pinned for visibility.
